dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A problem for a fixed law consists of two component-indexed real states, as exposed by D002, D003 and constructor D025.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Indexes the result family and supplies the left and right interface states.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first projection of a problem, its left state.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The interface problem at j has left state old(j−1).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second projection of a problem, its right state.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The interface problem at j has right state old(j).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The endpoints satisfy left < right, the field is interval integrable between them, and the designated average equals its normalized oriented integral.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each asserted spatial or temporal average includes positivity and integrability, not just an equality of totalized integral expressions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Every spatial slice of q is integrable on every finite interval; every fixed-position flux trace is integrable on every finite time interval; and every space-time rectangle satisfies the integral balance of state change against left flux minus right flux.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the substantive hypothesis on q; it supplies an exact integral conservation law for all real endpoints and times.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: An integer-indexed grid with real left and right cell endpoints, strictly positive widths, and matching adjacent endpoints, as specified by D026.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Restricts the grid to positive contiguous cells; supplies geometry for all averages and updates.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: The grid's left-endpoint function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Locates the left boundary of cell i and interface i.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The grid's right-endpoint function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Locates the right boundary of each cell and enters the adjacency equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: Cell volume is right endpoint minus left endpoint.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The update and error identities use actual positive cell length as their denominator or weight.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: A law packages a real vector flux, its derivative and representing Jacobian, and a real eigenbasis condition at every state, as specified by D027.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Quantification over laws implicitly requires global differentiability and pointwise real diagonalizability of the Jacobian.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: The physical-flux projection of a law.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The same flux appears in integral conservation, exact interface averages, and constant-state consistency.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: A method packages a problem domain, a domain-restricted solver, result extraction, numerical flux, admissibility of constant problems, and consistency on them, as specified by D028.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The method is an abstract consistent flux-producing pipeline, with results dependent on the problem.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: Every equal-left-and-right-state problem belongs to the method's domain.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the interface flux on any constant sequence well-defined without an additional domain hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: The method's predicate on admissible problems.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The supplied hdomain certifies all problems generated by old.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: The method's map from a result for any particular problem to Information.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the intermediate information used to produce an interface flux.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interface flux at j is numericalFlux applied to extract applied to the selected result at j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the numerical flux sequence used in the update and error estimates.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: The method's map from Information to a real state vector.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Converts extracted solver information into the numerical flux.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: The selected result at j is solve applied to the problem generated from old at j, using its domain proof.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The selected result is a specified solver output, not a newly existentially chosen result.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: The method's dependent solver: a problem and proof of admissibility produce an element of Result(problem).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Ensures results exist for admissible interface problems without asserting any further physical correctness.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: Builds the problem with left state old(j−1) and right state old(j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the adjacent-cell indexing and the problem on which each numerical flux depends.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: The integral over a region with restricted measure, multiplied by the inverse of the real conversion of that region's measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses cell and time averages as normalized integrals over left-open, right-closed intervals.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef022
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normalized interval integral of a state field between a cell's endpoints.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the exact spatial averages at s and t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef023
dependency_coverage.meaning: The update at i is old(i) minus timeStep/cellVolume(i) times edgeFlux(i+1)−edgeFlux(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the single conservative numerical update compared with q at time t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef024
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normalized time integral from s to t of the physical flux at the left endpoint of cell j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the exact flux average at interface j; adjacency identifies interface i+1 with cell i's right boundary.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef025
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a problem from an arbitrary pair of real state vectors.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Problem formation imposes no state admissibility condition beyond the separately supplied method domain.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef026
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a grid from endpoint functions and proofs that every cell has positive width and right(i−1)=left(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes cell positivity and interface matching structural assumptions on grid.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef027
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a law from F, continuous real-linear maps L(u), real matrices A(u), proofs that DF(u)=L(u), that L(u)v=A(u)v for all u,v, and that each A(u) has a real eigenbasis.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Restricts laws globally on the full real state space; no continuity of u↦L(u), distinct eigenvalues, or uniform diagonalization bound is supplied.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef028
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a method with domain, solve, extract and numericalFlux, together with domain membership and physical-flux agreement for every constant-state problem.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Constant consistency is already part of the input structure; general solver accuracy is not required.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef029
dependency_coverage.meaning: The average of f between a and b is (b−a)⁻¹ times the oriented interval integral of f.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes normalization for both spatial averages and exact temporal flux averages.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef030
dependency_coverage.meaning: There exist real eigenvalues indexed by the component type and a real basis of the state space, with each basis vector an eigenvector for its indexed eigenvalue.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires real diagonalizability at each state separately; witnesses may depend on the state and eigenvalues may repeat.

binders: For every natural number m and proof hm that 0<m, let V be the real vector space of functions Fin m→Real.
For every grid consisting of functions L,R:Z→R with L_i<R_i and R_{i−1}=L_i for every integer i.
For every law on V, including its flux F:V→V, derivative assignment and Jacobian assignment satisfying the structural conditions below.
For every type family Result indexed by problems for that law, and every type Information; their universes are arbitrary and independent.

For every method of the specified domain/solve/extract/numericalFlux structure, every old:Z→V, and every certificate hdomain asserting that the problem (old(j−1),old(j)) lies in the method domain for every j.
For every q:R→R→V, with first argument position and second argument time, satisfying the integral conservation predicate below.
For every pair of real times s,t with s<t.
The derivative conclusion quantifies over every real pair a,b, followed by almost every real time τ; the exceptional null set may depend on a,b.

The consistency conclusion quantifies over every state u∈V and every integer interface j. The interface-description conclusion quantifies over every integer j. The average, update and error conclusions quantify over every integer cell i.
Within each cell's error conclusion, oldBound, leftBound and rightBound are arbitrary real numbers, followed by three norm-bound hypotheses.
hypotheses: The grid has positive widths h_i=R_i−L_i and satisfies R_{i−1}=L_i for every i∈Z.
The law supplies a continuous real-linear map D(u):V→V and a real m×m matrix A(u) for every u∈V. F has Fréchet derivative D(u) at u, and D(u)v=A(u)v for every u,v∈V.
For every u∈V there exist real numbers λ_p indexed by p∈Fin m and a real basis (e_p) of V such that A(u)e_p=λ_p e_p for every p. Both the eigenvalue family and the basis may depend on u.
The method consists of a predicate domain on state-pair problems; solve(P,h)∈Result(P) for each P and h:domain(P); extract:Result(P)→Information for each P; and numericalFlux:Information→V.
For every u∈V, the constant problem C_u=(u,u) belongs to domain, and numericalFlux(extract(solve(C_u,constant-domain-proof)))=F(u).
For every j∈Z, hdomain(j) certifies domain(P_j), where P_j=(old(j−1),old(j)).
For every a,b,r∈R, x↦q(x,r) is Lebesgue interval integrable from a to b.
For every x,α,β∈R, τ↦F(q(x,τ)) is Lebesgue interval integrable from α to β.
For every a,b,α,β∈R, ∫_a^b q(x,β) dx−∫_a^b q(x,α) dx = ∫_α^β [F(q(a,τ))−F(q(b,τ))] dτ. All interval integrals are oriented.
conclusions: For every a,b∈R, for Lebesgue-almost every τ∈R, the function r↦∫_a^b q(x,r) dx has derivative F(q(a,τ))−F(q(b,τ)) at τ.
For every u∈V and j∈Z, the method's interface flux at j on the constant sequence k↦u, using its canonical constant-domain certificate, equals F(u).

For every j∈Z, let P_j=(old(j−1),old(j)) and r_j=solve(P_j,hdomain(j)). Then R_{j−1}=L_j, P_j.leftState=old(j−1), P_j.rightState=old(j), selectedResult(old,hdomain,j)=r_j, and interfaceFlux(old,hdomain,j)=numericalFlux(extract(r_j)). All five statements hold together.
For every i∈Z, L_i<R_i, the slice x↦q(x,s) is interval integrable on that cell, and Q_i(s)=h_i⁻¹∫_{L_i}^{R_i} q(x,s) dx.
For every i∈Z, L_i<R_i, the slice x↦q(x,t) is interval integrable on that cell, and Q_i(t)=h_i⁻¹∫_{L_i}^{R_i} q(x,t) dx.
For every i∈Z, Q_i(s) equals the normalized Lebesgue set integral over (L_i,R_i]: [volume((L_i,R_i]).toReal]⁻¹ ∫_{(L_i,R_i]} q(x,s) dx.
For every i∈Z, s<t, the trace τ↦F(q(L_i,τ)) is interval integrable from s to t, and G_i=(t−s)⁻¹∫_s^t F(q(L_i,τ)) dτ.
For every i∈Z, G_i also equals the normalized Lebesgue set integral [volume((s,t]).toReal]⁻¹∫_{(s,t]} F(q(L_i,τ)) dτ.
For every i∈Z, the defined numerical update U_i satisfies U_i=old(i)−((t−s)/h_i)(H_{i+1}−H_i).
For every i∈Z and every B_o,B_l,B_r∈R, if ‖old(i)−Q_i(s)‖∞≤B_o, ‖H_i−G_i‖∞≤B_l and ‖H_{i+1}−G_{i+1}‖∞≤B_r, then ‖U_i−Q_i(t)‖∞≤B_o+((t−s)/h_i)(B_l+B_r).
mathematical_definitions: V=R^{Fin m} has pointwise addition, subtraction and real scalar multiplication, the finite product topology, and norm ‖v‖∞=max_{p∈Fin m}|v(p)|.
A problem is a pair of vectors for the fixed law. No position, time, wave pattern or solution function is part of this problem data.
L_i=grid.cellLeft(i), R_i=grid.cellRight(i), and h_i=grid.cellVolume(i)=R_i−L_i. Interface j is the common point R_{j−1}=L_j.
For any suitable vector field f, Avg(f;a,b)=(b−a)⁻¹∫_a^b f. The predicate asserting that z is such an average also requires a<b and interval integrability of f.
For a measure μ and set S, SetAvg(μ,S,f)=((μ(S)).toReal)⁻¹∫ f d(μ restricted to S).
Q_i(r)=Avg(x↦q(x,r);L_i,R_i), the defined exact cell average at time r.
P_j=(old(j−1),old(j)), r_j=solve(P_j,hdomain(j)), and H_j=numericalFlux(extract(r_j)). H is the interface-flux sequence produced from old and its domain certificate.
G_j=Avg(τ↦F(q(L_j,τ));s,t), the exact physical-flux time average at interface j.
With Δ=t−s, U_i=old(i)−(Δ/h_i)(H_{i+1}−H_i), the defined one-step update.
The oriented Lebesgue integral ∫_a^b f is ∫_{(a,b]} f−∫_{(b,a]} f. Interval integrability means integrability on both of those sets.

The solver output r_j is a let-bound value depending on method, P_j and hdomain(j); it is not an existential witness in the conclusion. The only substantive existential witnesses in the expanded assumptions are the eigenvalues and eigenbasis separately available at every state.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive finite number of real state components, every positive-width contiguous integer-indexed grid, every globally differentiable flux law whose Jacobian has a real eigenbasis at each state, and every abstract domain-restricted solver/extraction/flux method consistent on constant states, take arbitrary old cell vectors whose adjacent-pair problems all lie in the method domain. Suppose q has integrable spatial slices and integrable physical-flux traces on all finite intervals and satisfies exact integral conservation on every real space-time rectangle. For any s<t, all the following hold simultaneously: the dimension is positive; each fixed spatial interval's state integral has time derivative equal to its left boundary flux minus its right boundary flux almost everywhere in time; constant input sequences produce the physical flux; each interface problem and flux have precisely the stated adjacent-state and solver-pipeline descriptions; the exact cell averages at both times and the exact interface flux time averages satisfy positivity, integrability and normalized-integral definitions, with the stated set-integral representations; the numerical update has its defining conservative flux-difference form; and its cell-width-weighted error is exactly the old weighted cell error plus the time increment times left flux error minus right flux error. Consequently, in each cell, any bounds on the old cell error and the two adjacent flux errors imply the stated maximum-norm bound on the updated error.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension must be positive. Zero-dimensional state spaces are excluded, and positivity is repeated in the conclusion.

The grid is integer-indexed with strictly positive real cell widths and exact adjacency. There is no uniform-spacing assumption, uniform lower width bound, or requirement that the cells cover the entire real line or that endpoints diverge at infinity.

The law's differentiability and real diagonalizability conditions hold on all of V. Eigenvalues need not be distinct, eigenbases need not be orthonormal, and their state dependence need not be continuous or uniformly controlled. Continuity of the derivative as a function of state is not required.

The method may have a proper domain. The conclusion applies to old only when every adjacent pair belongs to that domain. Constant problems must always be admissible, but arbitrary nonconstant pairs need not be.

Result and Information are abstract types. No condition says that a result solves a differential equation, represents waves, satisfies an entropy condition, or approximates an exact interface problem. Only the declared pipeline and constant-state flux consistency are encoded.
old is not assumed to equal or approximate Q(s). The final inequality is conditional on whatever cell and flux error bounds are supplied.

The hypothesis on q is a global integral rectangle identity for all real spatial endpoints and times, with integrability of every spatial slice and every pointwise flux trace. It is not merely a distributional equation or an almost-everywhere choice of spatial traces.
No pointwise spatial or temporal derivative of q, entropy admissibility, initial condition, boundary condition, or existence or uniqueness theorem for q is asserted.
The derivative assertion is ∀a,b, almost every τ. It does not assert one common full-measure set of times on which the derivative identity holds simultaneously for every a,b.

The time interval has s<t and all cell widths are positive. Thus the concrete normalization factors and update denominators are nonzero. Although the underlying inverse and integral definitions are totalized, the stated averages have genuine integrability and positive finite interval measures.

The bound variables range over all real numbers, with no separate nonnegativity assumptions. Their norm-bound premises force them to be nonnegative whenever those premises hold; choosing a negative bound makes the corresponding implication premise impossible.

The proposition gives a single-step exact error identity and conditional local norm estimate. It supplies no smallness estimates for flux errors, CFL restriction, monotonicity, convergence rate, multi-step stability theorem, or global spatial error bound.

Several conclusions unpack definitions or repeat properties already included in the input structures. In particular, constant consistency is assumed through method, and adjacency and width positivity are assumed through grid.
